key_points: Algebras over $\mathbf{P}\otimes\mathbf{Q}$ are equivalent to $\mathbf{Q}$-algebras in the category of $\mathbf{P}$-algebras
Equivalently, they are equivalent to $\mathbf{P}$-algebras in the category of $\mathbf{Q}$-algebras, so the order of nesting does not matter
question: What characterizing property does the Boardman–Vogt tensor product $\mathbf{P}\otimes\mathbf{Q}$ of two operads have in terms of categories of algebras?
atom_statement: For operads $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{Q}$, the Boardman–Vogt tensor product $\mathbf{P}\otimes\mathbf{Q}$ is an operad with the property that there are equivalences of categories $\mathrm{Alg}_{\mathbf{Q}}(\mathrm{Alg}_{\mathbf{P}}) \simeq \mathrm{Alg}_{\mathbf{P}\otimes\mathbf{Q}} \simeq \mathrm{Alg}_{\mathbf{P}}(\mathrm{Alg}_{\mathbf{Q}})$.
evidence: In this section we will deﬁne an operad P ⊗Q, the Boardman–Vogt tensor product of P and Q, which has the property that there are equivalences of categories
